attribs.name: repeating_traits_-OO9qKnqjGS1DjOqQXwV_description
attribs.current:
You have learned to channel the magical essence of nature to cast spells. See chapter 7 for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Ranger spells, which appear in the Ranger spell list later in the class's description.

Spell Slots. The Ranger Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Ranger spells. Cure Wounds and Ensnaring Strike are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Ranger levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Ranger Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Ranger spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the Ranger Features table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 5 Ranger, your list of prepared spells can include six Ranger spells of level 1 or 2 in any combination.

If another Ranger feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Ranger spells for you.

Changing Your Prepared Spells. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one spell on your list with another Ranger spell for which you have spell slots.

Spellcasting Ability. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Ranger spells.

Spellcasting Focus. You can use a Druidic Focus as a Spellcasting Focus for your Ranger spells.

attribs.name: repeating_traits_-OO9qKnuXJH43vp-8OZs_description
attribs.current:
Rangers are masters of the hunt, singling out prey out of a herd, isolating them and exploiting their weaknesses. You gain the following features:

Hunter's Mark: When you hit a creature with an attack, you can use your bonus action to mark them as your quarry for the next hour. When you do so, you have Advantage on any Wisdom (Perception or Survival) checks to track or find the creature. Your attacks also deal additional force damage equal to your Quarry die, which improves as shown in the ranger table.

If a creature dies while marked by you, you can immediately use your reaction or use your bonus action to move the mark on to another creature within your attack range (minimum of 60 feet).

You can use this feature twice, regaining one use on a Short Rest and all uses on a Long rest. You gain more uses of this feature as shown in the ranger table.

When you reach level 3 in this class, you no longer need to concentrate on the mark.

Mark Enhancements: When you apply a mark on a creature, you can choose to enhance it in various ways by expending an additional use of Ranger's quarry.

Blinding Mark: The marked creature has disadvantage on all checks that require sight.

Cardinal Mark: You know the direction of the creature as long as it is marked.

Elusive Mark: The marked creature has disadvantage on perception checks to detect you. Additionally, you can attempt to hide from the marked creature while behind half or three-fourths cover.

Illuminating Mark: The marked creature cannot benefit from the invisible or hidden condition against you.

Leashing Mark: The marked creature's movement speed is reduced by 10 feet if it is more than 60 feet away from you.

Pursuing Mark: You gain an additional 10 ft of movement speed when moving towards the marked creature.

Strafing Mark: When the marked creature enters within 10 feet of you, you can immediately use your reaction to move up to half of your movement speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

Blurring Mark: The marked creature has disadvantage on attack rolls against you.

Crippling Mark: The marked creature has disadvantage on all saving throws against you.

Focused Mark: Your attacks ignore disadvantage when attacking a marked creature.

Insightful Mark: You learn of any special senses (such as truesight or tremorsense) of the marked creature. Additionally, whenever the mark deals damage to the creature you learn whether it is resistant, vulnerable or immune to a single damage type or condition.

Rejuvenating Mark: You regain hitpoints equal to the damage dealt by hunter's mark.

Seismic Mark: The mark's damage is dealt in a 10 foot radius around the marked creature.

Unveiling Mark: You learn of any magic affecting the marked creature. You also learn of any magical items in its possession, although you do not learn the nature or properties of these items. Any effect that would block divination magic (such as the nondetection spell), will block this feature.

Vengeful Mark: When the marked creature deals damage to you, it takes force damage equal to your mark die. This damage is only dealt once per turn.

attribs.name: repeating_traits_-OO9qKo-n6WqicL3p8N3_description
attribs.current:
At 2nd level, you adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

Archery PHB'14 p72[–] You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with ranged weapons.

Blind Fighting TCE p41[–] You have blindsight with a range of 10 feet. Within that range, you can effectively see anything that isn't behind total cover, even if you're blinded or in darkness. Moreover, you can see an invisible creature within that range, unless the creature successfully hides from you.

Defense PHB'14 p72[–] While you are wearing armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC.

Druidic Warrior TCE p57[–] You learn two cantrips of your choice from the druid spell list. They count as ranger spells for you, and Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for them. Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can replace one of these cantrips with another cantrip from the druid spell list.

Dueling PHB'14 p72[–] When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.

Thrown Weapon Fighting TCE p42[–] You can draw a weapon that has the thrown property as part of the attack you make with the weapon.

In addition, when you hit with a ranged attack using a thrown weapon, you gain a +2 bonus to the damage roll.

Two-Weapon Fighting PHB'14 p72[–] When you engage in two-weapon fighting, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of the second attack.

attribs.current:
Rangers are masters of adaptation, surviving through harsh climates and dangerous foes alike. They do so by assimilating the skills into their core instinct.

You learn two imbibements of your choice at level 2. A list of available options can be found on the Optional Features page. When you gain ranger levels, you gain additional imbibements of your choice, as shown in the imbibements column of the ranger table.

Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the imbibements you know and replace it with another imbibement that you could learn at that level.

If a ranger imbibement has prerequisites, you must meet them to learn it. You can learn the imbibement at the same time that you meet its prerequisites. A level prerequisite refers to your level in this class.

3rd-level Hunter feature

You gain one of the following features of your choice. Whenever you finish a Short or Long Rest, you can replace the chosen option with the other one.

Colossus Slayer DRK p93[–] Your tenacity can wear down the most potent foes. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, the creature takes an extra 1d8 damage if it's below its hit point maximum. You can deal this extra damage only once per turn.

7th-level Hunter feature

You gain one of the following features of your choice. Whenever you finish a Short or Long Rest, you can replace the chosen option with the other one.

Escape the Horde DRK p1[–] You are difficult to pin down during a fight. As a reaction, when a hostile creature ends its turn within 5 ft. of you, you can move up to half your speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

For the duration of your turn after this, your movement speed is increased by 10 ft. and you have advantage on attacks against the triggering creature.

Nimble Movement DRK p93[–] When a creature attempts to attack you with a melee weapon attack, you can use your reaction to make a weapon attack at it before it's attack is made. If your attack hits, the creature's attack is then made at disadvantage.

This feature can be used a number of times equal to your Proficiency bonus, and you regain all of its expended uses when you finish a long rest.

Steel Will DRK p93[–] When you are subjected to a saving throw from a spell that deals damage, you can use your reaction to gain resistance against the spell's damage. You can use this feature twice, and you regain all expended uses on a long rest.

15th-level Hunter feature

You gain one of the following features of your choice. Whenever you finish a Short or Long Rest, you can replace the chosen option with the other one.

Multiattack Defense DRK p93[–] You are a master at learning the attack patterns of your foe.

You gain a +3 bonus to your AC per attack that a creature makes against you on their turn. This bonus lasts until the end of the creature's turn.

attribs.name: repeating_traits_-OOBZ49W89-ISHZ10VMt_description
attribs.current:
Wielding these blasters grants a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls, and each shot deals an additional 1d8 fire and cold damage depending on the pistol.
You must hold both the pistols in each hand, otherwise suffering a -10 penalty to attack rolls if used seperately. 
When you use an extra attack feature to an extra attack, you can use the other pistol to make an additional attack.

Infernal Leadfire. Twice per long rest, you may transform your weapon into a Tommy Gun or a Flamethrower for devastating effect. Upon transforming, roll 10d10 to determine the total bullet/fuel capacity for this form. While transformed, when you take the Attack action, you can replace one or more of your attacks with one of the following options based on the chosen form:
In Tommy Gun form, you can unleash a furious hail of bullets upon one or more targets within the weapon's range. As part of your Attack action, you may expend up to 20 bullets to fire a barrage. Each bullet deals 2 points of piercing damage. Each target must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC 20). On a successful save, it takes half damage instead. Alternatively, you can choose to dump the entire magazine shooting all the bullets, transforming it back into the blasters immediately.
In Flamethrower form, you expel gouts of searing flame in a wide arc. As part of your Attack action, you may expend up to 20 units of fuel to create a 60-foot cone of fire originating from you. Each creature within the cone must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC 20). A creature takes 1d8 fire damage per unit of fuel expended on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. For example, if you expend 10 units of fuel, each creature that fails the save suffers 10d fire damage.
This transformation ends if all bullets/fuel is consumed or one minute has passed.
Range. A weapon that can be used to make a ranged attack has a range shown in parentheses after the ammunition or thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second indicates the weapon's maximum range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the weapon's long range.
Ammunition. You can use a weapon that has the ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from the weapon. Each time you attack with the weapon, you expend one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition from a quiver, case, or other container is part of the attack. Loading a one-handed weapon requires a free hand. The ammunition of a firearm is destroyed upon use.
If you use a weapon that has the ammunition property to make a melee attack, you treat the weapon as an improvised weapon. A sling must be loaded to deal any damage when used in this way.
Reload. A limited number of shots can be made with a weapon that has the reload property. A character must then reload it using an action or a bonus action (the character's choice).

Concentration. You have Advantage on Constitution saving throws that you make to maintain Concentration.

Reactive Spell. When a creature provokes an Opportunity Attack from you by leaving your reach, you can take a Reaction to cast a spell at the creature rather than making an Opportunity Attack. The spell must have a casting time of one action and must target only that creature.

attribs.name: repeating_traits_-OOESiW89l22xhZAHGNd_description
attribs.current:
3.Ethereal Stride : As a reaction when you are targeted by an attack, you can enter the Ethereal Plane, move up to half your speed in any direction, and then return to your original plane. Entering the ethereal plane and moving through it does not provoke any opportunity attacks. You may use this feature as many times as your selected ability bonus. Uses recharge on a long rest.

4.Unholy Bargain : If you fall to 0 hit points, instead of falling unconscious, you can choose to remain conscious at 0 hit points as necrotic energy surges through your body. You do not need to make death saving throws. Everytime you take damage, you must make a constitution saving throw DC equal to half the damage taken or 10. On a failure, you receive a failed death saving throw. If you receive three failures, you immediately fall dead.
